h: Tactics, tables and a canal-side stroll
p: New to shuffleboard? Start gently. The best shots usually come from a smooth, relaxed push with a straight follow-through, letting the puck glide rather than flinging it. As you get the hang of the table's pace, try placing a blocker in front of your best puck, or aim to knock your opponent's puck out of the scoring zone. A few rounds in, you'll find yourself plotting like a chess grandmaster.

If you're planning a group outing, a little organisation helps. Book your table well ahead for weekends and the festive season, mix newcomers in with confident players, and sort the food order early so you're not juggling plates mid-game. Age policies can vary at social games bars, so check with the venue first if any of your group are under 18.

King's Cross has plenty to explore before or after. The British Library, just along Euston Road, is free to visit and its Treasures gallery displays some of the world's most important books and manuscripts. Camley Street Natural Park is a surprising patch of wildlife-filled green right beside the canal, and Gasholder Park, set inside a restored Victorian gasholder frame, is a striking place to sit with a coffee. You can also catch a canal boat trip along Regent's Canal, or walk the towpath west towards Camden Market for food and shopping. It's an area that rewards a wander, so give yourself a bit of spare time either side of your booking to soak it all up.
